title: Landscape fragmentation and agricultural context impact pollination services to native annual plants in critically endangered Australian woodlands
fragmentation_evidence: remnant size plus core-edge position in an agricultural mosaic; adjacent crop context also measured
eligible_layer_evidence: bee community/pollination service plus focal native-plant seed production on the same remnant system
decision_reason: The abstract explicitly links remnant size/edge fragmentation to bee communities and native-plant reproductive success. Full text is needed to recover remnant-level replication and confirm that the locked I and F endpoints share the same independent-unit frame.
next_action: recover remnant identities, replication, species handling and fragmentation-level I/F dispersion before any effect calculation

title: Habitat fragmentation affects plant–arthropod interactions through connectivity loss and edge effects
fragmentation_evidence: large replicated fragmentation experiment manipulating inter-patch connectivity and patch edge-to-area geometry
eligible_layer_evidence: pollinator visitation plus fruit-flower ratio in experimentally planted Carphephorus populations
decision_reason: This is an explicit replicated fragmentation experiment with a process endpoint and a reproductive endpoint measured in the same experimental system. Numerical admission still requires the experimental independent unit, endpoint definitions and compatible sampling dispersion.
next_action: recover treatment replication, experimental-unit IDs, visitation endpoint, fruit-flower endpoint and within-programme dependence

title: High selfing rate and inbreeding depression correlate with past range expansion in an endangered African timber species Pericopsis elata
fragmentation_evidence: fragmented distribution is historical/conservation context; focal comparison is SRI versus eastern genetic cluster and range expansion
eligible_layer_evidence: mating/selfing and inbreeding-depression/progeny information
decision_reason: The abstract does not analyze a source-defined fragmentation treatment or fragmentation-severity contrast. The focal inference concerns genetic clusters and past range expansion, so fragmentation cannot be manufactured as the exposure after screening.
next_action: retain as mating-system and range-history context only

title: Oak masting breaks down in a highly fragmented, pollen-limited landscape
fragmentation_evidence: continuous conspecific-neighbour isolation within one highly fragmented landscape over 11 years
eligible_layer_evidence: seed production is direct F; pollen limitation is central but the abstract does not establish an independently measured I endpoint
decision_reason: Fragmentation/isolation and seed production are directly studied, but the abstract may be interpreting pollen limitation from neighbour-dependent seed production rather than measuring an independent interaction endpoint. The screening contract sends this ambiguity to full text instead of excluding it.
next_action: verify whether pollen receipt, supplementation or another independent I measure exists and recover tree/landscape independent units

title: Pollinator Diversity and Pollen Flow of an Emergent Tropical Tree Species in a Fragmented Forest
fragmentation_evidence: six forest fragments spanning fragment size within one fragmented landscape
eligible_layer_evidence: pollinator assemblage and potential pollen-mass flow are measured; direct reproductive function is not demonstrated in the abstract
decision_reason: The publication is clearly fragmentation-relevant and directly measures I/C-type responses across six fragments. The abstract uses fecundity as motivation rather than reporting a direct F endpoint, so target-pair status is not assumed; full text can still establish admissible I/C layer effects or a missed F endpoint.
next_action: verify fragment-level replication, I/C endpoint dispersion and whether any direct F endpoint is actually measured

title: Floral morphs of a heterostylous grassland herb differ in responses to grassland fragmentation and environmental pressures
fragmentation_evidence: 30 semi-natural grassland populations differing in population size and habitat fragmentation
eligible_layer_evidence: seed production and offspring germination/performance are directly measured; direct I/C measurements are not established by the abstract
decision_reason: The study directly evaluates fragmentation across 30 populations and has clear reproductive/offspring endpoints. The abstract attributes patterns to pollination efficiency but does not establish direct pollinator or connectivity measurement, so pair membership is withheld pending methods review.
next_action: recover fragmentation metric, population-level F/G_offspring endpoints and check for any direct I/C measurements

title: An isolated, yet extensive population of the threatened species Jacobaea paludosa (Asteraceae) shows alarming reproductive constraints
fragmentation_evidence: one focal isolated population plus comparison to a population subjected to reinforcement; habitat loss is background
eligible_layer_evidence: pollination dependence/limitation tests and direct fruit, seed-vitality and germination fitness endpoints
decision_reason: I and F are directly measured, but the abstract does not show that the focal-versus-reinforced population comparison is a source-defined fragmentation exposure. Ambiguity therefore advances to full-text clarification rather than being treated as a valid I-F contrast.
next_action: verify population identities, whether fragmentation/isolation is the comparison variable, and independent replication

title: Mating Matters: The Breeding System and Effects of Inbreeding and Outbreeding in the Endangered Willamette Daisy
fragmentation_evidence: isolated remnant populations motivate the study but controlled crosses compare mating treatments and local versus distant pollen
eligible_layer_evidence: breeding-system crosses, seed set and offspring growth
decision_reason: The experimental exposure is pollination/cross type, not habitat fragmentation. Isolation is conservation context, and local-versus-distant crosses cannot be recoded as fragmented-versus-reference habitat units.
next_action: retain as reproductive-assurance and genetic-mixing context only

title: Breeding System of Jacquemontia curtisii, an Endemic Morning-Glory of Pine Rocklands
fragmentation_evidence: pine-rockland habitat fragmentation is conservation context; study plants are grown in greenhouse and exposed to hand-pollination treatments
eligible_layer_evidence: breeding-system and fruit-set responses to pollination treatments
decision_reason: The study does not compare fragmentation exposures. Its causal treatments are greenhouse/hand-pollination breeding-system treatments, so fragment size or isolation cannot be inferred as the exposure from the conservation discussion.
next_action: retain as breeding-system context only

title: Assessment of genetic conservation units of an endangered glacial relict insular species, Amentotaxus formosana, based on fine-scale genetic structures of multiple fragmented mountainous populations in Taiwan
fragmentation_evidence: three mountainous regions contain fragmented/discontinuous populations; exact fragmentation-severity contrast is not specified in the abstract
eligible_layer_evidence: genetic diversity, structure, inbreeding and gene flow are measured; direct reproductive function is not reported
decision_reason: The study is clearly about fragmented populations and directly measures C/G-type responses, but the abstract does not provide an eligible F endpoint or an explicit source-defined fragmentation contrast. Full text is needed to decide whether it contributes a gradient/single-layer effect rather than a C-F pair.
next_action: recover fragmentation metric, independent population units and C/G endpoint summaries; verify whether any direct F endpoint exists

title: Inbreeding Depression Manifested in Progeny From Fragmented Populations of the Wind-Pollinated Dioecious Conifer Afrocarpus gracilior
fragmentation_evidence: multiple small/isolated versus larger populations are explicitly central to the fragmentation study
eligible_layer_evidence: direct reproductive/progeny-fitness endpoints are reported; direct movement/connectivity C is not established by the abstract
decision_reason: The study directly tests fragmentation-associated genetic/reproductive consequences across populations and has clear progeny fitness. Full text is needed to verify whether a movement/connectivity endpoint exists on the same population frame rather than inferring C from genetic state.
next_action: recover population frame, fragmentation metric, C if directly estimated, and F/G_offspring endpoint units

title: A Spatial Structure of Key Tree Species Metrodorea nigra Is Associated with Historical Disturbance and Isolation in Southeastern Brazil
fragmentation_evidence: three fragmented populations with different disturbance/matrix/fragment size
eligible_layer_evidence: adult/juvenile genetic state is measured across populations; phenology/germination are evaluated only in BSQ; pollinator behaviour is explanatory rather than directly measured
decision_reason: The multilayer metadata hit conflates population-wide genetic comparisons with phenology/germination measured in a single fragment and inferred pollinator behaviour. No common I-F or C-F fragmentation frame is supported by the abstract.
next_action: retain adult/juvenile genetic fragmentation evidence; no target-pair admission

title: Reduced rodent-mediated seed dispersal at forest edge hinders regeneration
fragmentation_evidence: four source-defined edge-to-interior distances: 0, 20, 40 and 60 m
eligible_layer_evidence: rodent-mediated seed removal/scatter-hoarding/dispersal plus subsequent seedling establishment/regeneration
decision_reason: The study directly measures a movement/dispersal process across an edge gradient and follows regeneration. Full text must establish experimental replication and whether F/recruitment contains enough independent information for a paired gradient effect.
next_action: recover replicate stations/plots, locked C endpoint, recruitment endpoint and common edge-distance frame

title: The abundance and reproductive success of the orchid Calypso bulbosa L. in relation to forest structure
fragmentation_evidence: forest interior/opening/clear-cut proximity and population-size structure over seven years
eligible_layer_evidence: pollinated plants and flower/fruit production are observed, but direct visitor-service measurement is unclear
decision_reason: The source is explicitly framed around forest structure/fragmentation and reproduction. The abstract does not resolve whether pollination is directly measured and whether the exposure is habitat geometry versus population size, so ambiguity advances to methods review.
next_action: verify site/population replication, direct I measurement and source-defined fragmentation predictor

title: Flowering and Fruiting Characteristics and Phenology of an Endemic Monoecious Tree in a Fragmented African Rainforest Landscape
fragmentation_evidence: three fragments under 30 ha versus three continuous-forest sites
eligible_layer_evidence: flower/fruit phenology and floral production are measured; no movement/connectivity endpoint is reported
decision_reason: The six-site fragmentation contrast is strong, but the abstract contains no pollen/seed movement, gene-flow, parentage or dispersal-connectivity C endpoint. C-F membership is a metadata false positive.
next_action: retain reproductive/phenological fragmentation evidence; no C-F pair admission

title: Impact of fragmented habitats on reproductive success in dominant shrubs: natural selection on floral display and pollinator visitation
fragmentation_evidence: source explicitly compares natural and fragmented habitats
eligible_layer_evidence: pollinator visitation frequency and female fitness/pollen limitation are directly measured
decision_reason: The abstract establishes a direct habitat comparison and directly measured interaction and reproductive-function endpoints. This is a high-priority same-system I-F candidate pending independent-unit and dispersion verification.
next_action: recover habitat replication, population/plot identities, visitation and female-fitness endpoints plus dependence

title: The interplay between local biodiversity floral odours and reproductive success varies across different population sizes of Cypripedium calceolus
fragmentation_evidence: fragmentation motivates comparison of small versus large orchid populations; population size is the analysed predictor
eligible_layer_evidence: visitor diversity and reproductive success are measured
decision_reason: The tested contrast is small versus large population size, not a source-defined habitat fragmentation treatment or response-free fragmentation geometry. Population size is not recoded as fragmentation after screening.
next_action: retain population-size/Allee context; no direct EGWEE fragmentation pair

title: A comprehensive dataset on pollinator diversity, visitation rates, individual-based traits, and pollination success across four plant species in an urban garden experiment in Zurich, Switzerland
fragmentation_evidence: 24 gardens vary in proportion impervious surface at 500 m, a source-defined urban-intensity/habitat-loss gradient
eligible_layer_evidence: flower visitation/richness and seed/fruit set are directly available in the same experimental garden system
decision_reason: The dataset supplies direct I and F responses with a predeclared landscape habitat-loss proxy. It is not a binary fragment/reference design but may enter the registered gradient/generalisation stream if garden-level units and common species frames are recoverable.
next_action: inspect raw dataset schema, garden-level exposure, species overlap and paired I/F values

title: Phenology, floral biology, morphology and hawkmoth pollination of Calliandra magdalenae in modified landscapes of the Soconusco region, Mexico
fragmentation_evidence: modified-landscape/habitat-fragmentation context; no explicit comparative fragmentation treatment or gradient in abstract
eligible_layer_evidence: pollinator observations and low fruit set are measured; pollen dispersal is stated as a potential benefit rather than directly estimated
decision_reason: The study characterizes phenology, floral biology, pollinators and reproduction in modified landscapes, but the abstract does not define a fragmentation treatment/gradient across independent units. C is also interpretive rather than measured.
next_action: retain pollination/reproductive natural-history context only

title: Plant Mating Systems in Small Populations
fragmentation_evidence: review of small-population and fragmentation theory/evidence
eligible_layer_evidence: review synthesis rather than a new primary fragmentation programme
decision_reason: This is an Annual Review article, not an independent primary study. It can inform interpretation and citation discovery but cannot contribute a programme effect.
next_action: retain as background/citation-discovery source only
